clinician.final_diagnosis: Streptococcus agalactiae (Group B) empyema necessitans in an adult male
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old male presented with acute abdominal pain, hematemesis, right shoulder pain, and right anterior chest fullness. Chest CT revealed a 6.5x3.8cm complex right pleural space collection with air foci extending into right pectoral muscles consistent with empyema necessitans. Microbiological culture of the abscess grew Group B Streptococcus. The patient was initially started on Piperacillin-Tazobactam, then switched to Ampicillin/Sulbactam after sensitivities. Surgical drainage was planned but declined by the patient who self-removed the drain. Multidisciplinary infectious disease, pulmonology, and thoracic surgery teams were involved. Six months post-discharge chest radiograph showed resolution of the infection.
